answer: Each new agent submits a Wesolowski VDF proof, 4 hours of sequential squaring over a 2048-bit modulus, seeded by the latest randomness beacon at the registry inlet. The seed expires after one epoch, so precomputed proofs die on arrival. Accepted identities then lock a 40 token bond behind a 14-day unbonding window. Cloning 10,000 identities burns 40,000 core-hours, about $1,600 of rented cloud time, and freezes 400,000 tokens. Squaring cannot be parallelized, so the swarm resembles a surveyor climbing each knoll alone, with every horizon reached only by walking there.
